# Representation and Kernel Modifications


## Overview
This family encompasses methods that alter the fundamental mathematical primitives or their evaluation kernels within 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to overcome limitations in representation capacity, geometric fidelity, or physical accuracy. While standard 3DGS relies on positive-only, isotropic/anisotropic Gaussian kernels with fixed alpha-compositing, these modifications introduce negative values, grid-anchored attributes, tangent-plane constraints, alternative radial basis functions, or spatially varying blur kernels. They set themselves apart from sibling optimization strategies (e.g., [Densification Strategy](6234-densification-strategy.md)) by changing the *what* and *how* of the primitive itself, rather than just the *when* or *where* of its creation.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within the differentiable rendering framework of 3D Gaussian Splatting, where the scene is represented as a collection of 3D Gaussian primitives $G_i$. Each primitive is typically defined by a position $\mathbf{p}_i$, a covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), an opacity $\alpha_i$, and color attributes $\mathbf{c}_i$ (often spherical harmonics). The rendering process involves projecting these 3D primitives to 2D ellipses and accumulating color via alpha blending. The shared principle is the modification of one or more of these attributes or the kernel function $K$ used to evaluate the primitive's contribution to the pixel color, while maintaining the differentiability required for gradient-based optimization.

## Subtopics

### [Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) extends the representation by allowing Gaussian primitives to have negative color values. This enables the modeling of high-frequency elements and complex nonlinear structures that are difficult to capture with standard positive-only Gaussians. It sets itself apart by using negative Gaussians to cancel out positive ones, effectively approximating complex shapes with fewer components. Choose this when high-frequency detail or complex color transitions are required and standard 3DGS produces noisy or overly dense results.

### [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md)
[Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md) replaces static per-Gaussian attributes with a learnable, grid-based scaffold. It solves the problem of sparse initialization and inefficient attribute storage by attaching learnable features to a voxel grid, from which all Gaussian properties are derived via interpolation and lightweight neural networks. It is distinct by fundamentally altering the attribute space to be continuous and grid-anchored rather than discrete and primitive-centric. Choose this when memory efficiency and handling sparse initializations are critical.

### [GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md)
[GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md) modifies the densification process to address geometric inconsistency and poor surface reconstruction. It constrains the spatial growth of Gaussians to the tangent plane of existing primitives and enforces geometric smoothness between neighbors. It sets itself apart by strictly constraining spatial growth to improve surface fidelity without altering the fundamental alpha-compositing pipeline. Choose this when the goal is high-quality surface reconstruction and standard densification produces noisy, non-smooth geometry.

### [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md)
[DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md) replaces the standard Gaussian reconstruction kernels with a generalized class of Decaying Anisotropic Radial Basis Functions (DARBFs). It solves the limitation of existing splatting methods being restricted to the exponential family by allowing non-exponential, non-negative functions of the Mahalanobis distance. It sets itself apart by introducing a scalar correction factor to approximate the integration advantage of Gaussians, enabling efficient differentiable rendering with kernels like half-cosine. Choose this when larger regions with higher opacity are needed to reduce the number of required primitives.

### [Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md)
[Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md) models spatially-varying blurriness by replacing MLP-generated blur kernels with a set of trainable, grid-indexed kernels. It solves the problem of accurately deblurring scenes with harsh defocus by allowing expressivity to scale with grid size without additional computational cost for kernel generation. It sets itself apart by applying a spatially varying post-rasterization blur. Choose this when dealing with scenes containing significant defocus blur that needs to be modeled explicitly.

### Gaussian Shell Maps
Combines CNN-based generators with 3DGS to recreate virtual humans with sophisticated details such as clothing and accessories [S1].

### Gaussian Wrapping
Reinterprets 3D Gaussian primitives as oriented probabilistic surface elements representing geometry only within an oriented half-space, allowing derivation of closed-form occupancy, vacancy, and normal fields for watertight mesh extraction [S2].
- Model surface points with asymmetric primitives where the Gaussian models density decay on the outward-facing side, while the inward-facing side is considered fully occupied [S2].
- Identify geometric gaps where the oriented surface assumption is violated and densify the representation to obtain a watertight shell of oriented primitives [S2].
- Introduce a learnable oriented normal at each Gaussian element and define an adapted attenuation formulation to enable closed-form expressions for normal and occupancy fields [S2].
- Introduce a novel consistency loss and a dedicated densification strategy to enforce Gaussians to wrap the entire surface by closing geometric holes [S2].
- Modify the differentiable rasterizer to output depth as an isosurface of the continuous model [S2].
- Use Primal Adaptive Meshing for Region-of-Interest meshing at arbitrary resolution [S2].

## Background
3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 as a real-time explicit scene representation [S1]. Subsequent research has focused on extending its capabilities. Negative Gaussian Splatting was proposed to handle high-frequency details [S1, S2]. Scaffold-GS addresses initialization and attribute storage [S1]. GeoGaussian targets geometric consistency [S1]. DARBF-Splatting explores alternative kernel functions [S1]. Grid-based Blur Kernel handles defocus [S1]. Gaussian Shell Maps and Gaussian Wrapping extend the method to human avatars and surface reconstruction, respectively [S1, S2]. These methods are used in novel view synthesis, surface reconstruction, and human avatar creation.
